disposition_reason: Lead and other trace metals were measured by ICP-OES in oil extracted from French fries bought from two UK fast-food chains; Table 4 gives µg/kg of extracted oil and Table 7 µg per 30 g serving. Per owner instruction only lead is extracted.

study.design: Real-world sampling of French fries from two fast-food chain restaurants on three days at three times of day
study.market: two global chain fast-food restaurants (X and Y), UK
study.period_text: 30 November, 1 December and 3 December 2018 (morning, afternoon, evening)
study.method: Oil extracted from fries with n-hexane; 0.5 g oil microwave-digested with HNO3/H2O2; ICP-OES
study.lod_text: LOQ not given numerically in main text (Supplementary Table 1)
study.qa: Reagent blanks; duplicate digests; multi-element calibration 0-50,000 µg/kg; no CRM reported

controls.outcome: Pb in fry oil extract overall 76.79 (Y) vs 175.32 µg/kg (X); about 2-fold lower in Y

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Daily maximum Pb per 77.5 kg body weight used by authors (EFSA-derived)

unresolved: Owner instruction: lead only. Table 4 and Table 7 also print Al, Ba, Cd, Cr, Cu, Fe, Mn, Ni, Ti, V and Zn; these were not extracted.
Results are for the n-hexane oil extract of fries, not for whole fries; Table 7 per-serving values are derived by the authors.
LOQ values are in Supplementary Table 1, not available.
